campaigns.title: Oil Consumption Inspection (Customer Satisfaction Notification)
campaigns.summary: 2015-2018 Jeep Renegade (FWD only — AWD Renegades are NOT covered by this notification), 2016-2018 Fiat 500X (FWD/AWD), and 2015-2018 Ram ProMaster City with the 2.4L engine (sales codes ED6/ED8/EDD/EDE) may exhibit excessive oil consumption from a combination of manufacturing variances and the engine calibration strategy, affecting ~241,000 vehicles; unaddressed, a low oil condition can eventually cause a stall. The dealer procedure: top off oil, drive a monitored 1500-1700 miles, recheck the level after a 5-minute hot shutdown on level ground. Below the ADD mark = failed test -> long-block engine replacement.
campaigns.reference: NHTSA TSB doc MC-10220586-9999 (FCA Dealer Service Instructions, Customer Satisfaction Notification W80 — Oil Consumption Inspection, Rev. 2 Feb 2021). Verified 2026-09-26 against the primary-source PDF at static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2021/MC-10220586-9999.pdf.
steps: Top off oil to the full mark
Recheck level after a 5-minute hot shutdown on level ground
Below the ADD mark = failed test → long-block engine replacement

campaigns.title: PCM Reprogramming for Oil Consumption
campaigns.summary: Customer Satisfaction Notification W84 (Powertrain Software Update) is narrower than W80: verified against the primary source, it covers only 2014 (KL) Jeep Cherokee, 2017 (UF) Chrysler 200, 2017 (MP) Jeep Compass, 2017 (KL) Jeep Cherokee, and 2017 (BU) Jeep Renegade AWD — all with the 2.4L engine (ED6/ED8/EDD/EDE). It does NOT cover Fiat 500X, Ram ProMaster City, or Renegade FWD/any model year outside 2014 or 2017. Reprograms the PCM and TCM and clears DTCs; does not itself require the oil consumption test in W80.
campaigns.reference: NHTSA TSB doc MC-10215923-9999 (FCA Dealer Service Instructions, Customer Satisfaction Notification W84 — Powertrain Software Update, Jan 2021). Verified 2026-09-26 against the primary-source PDF at static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2021/MC-10215923-9999.pdf. NOTE: this corrects an earlier unverified entry that assumed W84 shared W80's 2015-2018/FWD Renegade/500X/ProMaster City scope — it does not.
steps: Verify VIN applicability with a dealer
Apply the PCM software update for oil-consumption behavior when applicable

campaigns.title: Brake Hydro-Boost Relief Valve (GM Recall No. 04004)
campaigns.summary: Certain SUVs, pickup trucks, and passenger vans — including the 2003 Chevrolet Silverado — were produced with an out-of-specification brake hydro-boost housing relief valve bore. The valve O-ring seal may fracture, requiring a slight increase in brake pedal effort or steering effort while braking. ~68,875 units affected across covered models/years.
campaigns.reference: NHTSA recall campaign 04V045000, GM Recall No. 04004, reported 2004-04-02. Verified 2026-09-26 directly against NHTSA's recall database (api.nhtsa.gov/recalls/campaignNumber?campaignNumber=04V045000), filtered to Make=CHEVROLET, Model=SILVERADO, ModelYear=2003 — a confirmed match. Manufacturer of record: General Motors Corp.
steps: Dealer replaces the hydro-boost relief valve
No owner action beyond scheduling the recall repair

campaigns.title: Tailgate Support Cable Corrosion (GM Recall No. 04007)
campaigns.summary: On certain pickup trucks and SUVs — including the 2003 Chevrolet Silverado — the galvanized steel tailgate support cables that hold the tailgate open may corrode, weaken, and fracture; if both cables fail the tailgate can drop suddenly onto the rear bumper. A very large recall (~3.66 million units across covered models/years).
campaigns.reference: NHTSA recall campaign 04V129000, GM Recall No. 04007, reported 2004 (interim notice 2004-04-07; recall began 2004-09-24). Verified 2026-09-26 directly against NHTSA's recall database (api.nhtsa.gov/recalls/campaignNumber?campaignNumber=04V129000), filtered to Make=CHEVROLET, Model=SILVERADO, ModelYear=2003 — a confirmed match. Manufacturer of record: General Motors Corp.
steps: Dealer replaces the tailgate support cables

campaigns.title: Parking Brake Friction Lining Wear — Manual Transmission Only (GM Recall No. 05042)
campaigns.summary: CONDITIONAL — applies only if this specific truck has a manual transmission with a PBR or TRW parking brake system (transmission type is not decodable from the VIN; this profile does not record it). On qualifying trucks, parking brake friction linings may wear enough for the parking brake to become ineffective at holding the vehicle. ~90,242 units affected across covered models/years.
campaigns.reference: NHTSA recall campaign 05V161000, GM Recall No. 05042, recall began 2005-07-29. Verified 2026-09-26 directly against NHTSA's recall database (api.nhtsa.gov/recalls/campaignNumber?campaignNumber=05V161000), filtered to Make=CHEVROLET, Model=SILVERADO, ModelYear=2003 — a confirmed match, but the manual-transmission condition itself is unverified against this specific vehicle. Manufacturer of record: General Motors Corp.
steps: Confirm the truck has a manual transmission before assuming this applies
PBR system: dealer installs a low-force spring clip retainer
TRW system: dealer installs a redesigned parking brake cable assembly

tsbs.title: MultiAir Actuator Assembly Diagnostic Procedure (2.4L Tigershark Only)
tsbs.summary: When diagnosing P-codes related to the MultiAir unit, the required check order is: (1) verify engine oil is not low, (2) verify the oil filter meets OEM spec, (3) verify oil is not dirty/deteriorated, (4) verify correct oil viscosity/weight, (5) verify oil is not contaminated (coolant/fuel), (6) verify the oil galley screen/filter feeding the MultiAir unit is not clogged — BEFORE replacing the MultiAir actuator itself.
tsbs.reference: FCA GPOP Issue Review System tech tip, document MC-10228154-9999, dated 8/10/2016, for MY14-16 PF/KL/BU/UF platforms. Note: "05047457A" is the MultiAir actuator assembly PART NUMBER this tip is filed under, not a separate TSB bulletin number. Verified 2026-09-26 against the primary-source PDF at static.nhtsa.gov/odi/tsbs/2016/MC-10228154-9999.pdf — the six-item pre-check order matches this ontology's steps verbatim.
steps: Verify engine oil is not low
Verify the oil filter meets OEM spec
Verify the oil galley screen/filter feeding the MultiAir unit is not clogged
Only then consider MultiAir actuator replacement
